# AF 第三章 原文（重制基线）

## Chapter 3

[P01] How they worked and sweated（出汗了） to get the hay（干草） in! But they were rewarded, for the harvest was even bigger than they hoped. Sometimes the work was hard, because the tools were made for people, not animals. No animal could use a tool that needed standing on two back legs. But the pigs were clever and found a way around every problem. The horses knew the field well and understood mowing（割草） and raking（耙草） better than Jones and his men ever did.

[P02] The pigs did not work. They told the others what to do and led them. Boxer and Clover pulled the cutter（切割机） or the horse-rake（耙子）. No bits or reins（缰绳） were needed. They walked round and round the field. A pig walked behind and called "Gee（驾） up, comrade（同志）!" or "Whoa（停） back, comrade!" Every animal helped turn the hay and gather（收集） it. Even the ducks and hens worked all day, carrying little bits of hay in their beaks（鸟嘴）.

[P03] In the end they finished the harvest two days faster than Jones and his men usually did. Moreover, it was the biggest harvest the farm had ever had. Nothing was wasted. The hens and ducks picked up the very last stalk（茎）. And no animal stole even one mouthful（一口）. It was a big problem that no animal could use any tool that needed standing on his hind（后面的） legs. But they found a way round every difficulty. The pigs supervised（监督） and led the work. The horses pulled the cutter and rake. The pigs called "Gee up!" or "Whoa back!" as needed. Even the smallest animals helped. All through that summer the work went like clockwork（钟表）.

[P04] The animals were happier than they ever thought possible. Every bite was a joy, because the food was truly their own. They grew it themselves, and no master gave it to them. With the humans gone, there was more food and more rest for everyone. They still had problems. When they harvested the corn, they had no machine. They had to crush（压碎） it by walking on it and blow the chaff（谷壳） away. But the pigs were clever, and Boxer was strong, so they helped the animals get through.

[P05] Boxer was admired by everyone. He worked hard even when Jones was master. Now he seemed as strong as three horses. Some days, all the farm work rested on his big shoulders. He always worked where the job was hardest. He asked a young rooster（公鸡） to wake him half an hour earlier. Then he did extra（额外） work before the day began. His answer to every problem was, "I will work harder!" He made this his motto.

[P06] The hens and ducks gathered（聚集） stray（走失） grains（谷物） and saved five bushels（蒲式耳） of corn at harvest. Nobody stole or complained. The quarrelling（争吵） and biting of the old days had almost gone. Nobody was idle—or almost nobody. Mollie often left work early, saying there was a stone（石头） in her hoof（蹄）. The cat was also strange. When there was work, the cat could never be found.

[P07] She would go away for hours, then come back at meal-times, as if nothing had happened. But she had such good excuses, and purred（咕噜叫） so sweetly, that everyone believed she meant well. Old Benjamin, the donkey, seemed the same since the uprising（起义）. He worked as slow and stubborn（固执） as in Jones's time. He never avoided work, and never did more than he had to. About the uprising he said nothing. When people asked if he was happier now that Jones was gone, he would only say, "Donkeys live a long time."

[P08] He would only say, "Donkeys live a long time. None of you has ever seen a dead donkey." The others had to accept this strange answer. On Sundays there was no work. Breakfast was an hour later than usual. After breakfast there was a ceremony every week. First they put up the flag. Snowball had found an old green tablecloth（桌布） of Mrs. Jones's. He had painted a hoof and a horn on it in white.

[P09] Every Sunday morning, they raised the flag in the farmhouse（农舍） garden. The flag was green, Snowball said, to stand for the fields of England. The hoof and horn meant the future Republic（共和国） of the Animals, which would come when humans were beaten. Then all the animals went into the big barn（谷仓） for a Meeting. Here they planned the next week's work and talked about resolutions. It was always the pigs who put forward the resolutions. The other animals could vote, but could never think of any of their own.

[P10] Snowball and Napoleon were the most active in the debates. But people noticed these two never agreed. If one made a suggestion, the other always opposed（反对） it. Even when everyone agreed to set aside（旁边） the small field behind the orchard（果园） as a rest home for old animals, they argued about the right retiring（退休） age for each kind of animal. The Meeting always ended with the song 'Beasts（野兽） of England', and the afternoon was for play. The pigs had set aside the harness（马具）-room as their headquarters（总部）.

[P11] In the evenings, the pigs studied blacksmithing（打铁） and carpentering（木工活） from books from the farmhouse. Snowball was always busy. He put the other animals into groups called Animal Committees（委员会） — for the hens, the cows, and to tame（驯服） the rats and rabbits. He also started classes in reading and writing. But most of these ideas failed, and the plan to tame the wild animals failed almost at once.

[P12] They went on as before. When others were kind, they just used it. The cat joined the Re-education Committee（委员会） and was busy for days. One day she sat on a roof and talked to some sparrows（麻雀）, too far to catch. She told them all animals were comrades（同志们） now, and any sparrow（麻雀） could sit on her paw（爪子）. But the sparrows stayed away. The reading and writing classes went very well. By autumn almost every animal could read and write a little. The pigs could already read and write well.

[P13] The dogs learned to read, but only liked the Seven Commandments（戒律）. Muriel the goat read better than the dogs. She sometimes read old newspapers to the others in the evening. Benjamin could read as well as any pig, but he never did. He said there was nothing worth reading. Clover learned all the letters, but could not make words. Boxer stopped at D. He would write A, B, C, D in the dust（灰尘） with his big hoof (蹄子), then stand and look at them, trying to remember the next letter and never doing it.

[P14] Many times he did learn E, F, G, H, but then he always found he had forgotten A, B, C, and D. At last he decided to keep only the first four letters. He wrote them once or twice every day to help his memory. Mollie would not learn any letters but the six that spelt（拼写） her own name. She made these neatly（整洁地） with small sticks, put a flower or two on them, and walked round them, happy with her work.

[P15] Some animals, like the sheep, hens and ducks, were too stupid to learn the Seven Commandments. Snowball said they could be put into one saying: "Four legs good, two legs bad." He said this held the main idea of Animalism（动物主义）. The birds objected, because they thought they had two legs too. But Snowball showed them they did not.

[P16] So a bird's wing is a leg. Man is different because of his HAND. He uses his hands to do bad things." The birds did not understand Snowball's long words, but they agreed. All the less clever animals worked hard to learn the saying by heart. FOUR LEGS GOOD, TWO LEGS BAD was written on the end wall of the barn, above the Seven Commandments and in bigger letters. Once the sheep learned it, they liked it very much, and often when they lay in the field they would all start bleating "Four legs good, two legs bad!"

[P17] "Four legs good, two legs bad!" and they would say it for hours. Napoleon did not care about Snowball's committees. He said teaching the young was more important. Jessie and Bluebell had their puppies soon after the hay harvest. Together they had nine strong puppies. As soon as the puppies stopped drinking milk, Napoleon took them away. He said he would take care of their education. He took them up to a loft（阁楼）. You could only reach it by a ladder from the harness-room（挽具室）. He kept them hidden there, and soon the other animals forgot about them. The mystery of where the milk went was soon solved.

[P18] The milk was mixed into the pigs' mash（糊状饲料） every day. The early apples were ripe（成熟）, and the grass was covered with fallen apples. The animals thought these would be shared equally. But one day, all the fallen apples must be collected and brought to the harness-room（挽具室） for the pigs. Some animals murmured（低语）, but it was no use. All the pigs agreed, even Snowball and Napoleon. Squealer was sent to explain. "Comrades!" he cried.

[P19] "You do not think, I hope, that we pigs do this because we are selfish? Many of us do not like milk and apples. I do not like them myself. We take these things only to keep healthy. Milk and apples (Science has proved this, comrades) have things that a pig must have to be well. We pigs are brainworkers（脑力劳动者）. All the work of running this farm depends on us. Do you know what would happen if we pigs failed in our duty?

[P20] "Jones would come back! Yes, Jones would come back! Surely, comrades," cried Squealer, almost begging（乞求）, jumping from side to side and moving his tail, "surely none of you wants to see Jones come back?" Now the animals were sure of one thing: they did not want Jones back. When they saw it this way, they had nothing more to say. It was clear that the pigs must stay healthy. So they agreed, with no more arguing, that the milk and the fallen apples (and also the main apples when they were ripe) should be kept for the pigs only.
